description: Borrow the iterative belief-propagation concept from LDPC/Turbo code decoders to design a two-pass Base64 validation scheme: a fast first pass decodes optimistically, while a lightweight second pass propagates belief about character validity backward from padding. Separates fast path (no errors) from slow path (error localization).
mathematical_formalization: Pass 1: decoded = lookup(input); error_flag |= has_invalid(decoded). Pass 2 (only if error_flag): binary search for error position. Cost: C_decode + 0 (common case) or O(log N) probes.
analogical_connections: LDPC decoding: separate variable-node and check-node updates
Speculative execution: execute past branches, rollback on mispredict
Optimistic concurrency control: proceed without locks, validate at commit
implementation_hypothesis: Accumulate error flags into a 64-bit mask. If zero after processing, validation passes with zero overhead. If nonzero, use _tzcnt_u64 to find the first errored block.
experiment_seed: Benchmark: (1) all-valid input, (2) error at byte 0, (3) error at last byte. Target: scenario 1 identical to no-validation decode.
